answer: Behavioral Grove Clustering. Agents are grouped into a grove by long-run overlap in the idiosyncratic transaction relic records they leave across unrelated services; isolated identities that only interact within one cluster are flagged retroactively. Enforcement: clusters whose internal recurrence exceeds a threshold get their identities' payouts frozen pending review. Cost: an attacker must fabricate sustained cross-service histories per identity, and any wander outside the cluster breaks the overlap, forcing costly re-establishment per sybil.
